answer: One concrete Sybil defense is identity-bound staking with slashing. Each agent must lock a bond before it can claim a wallet, and peers attest that the identity performs real work. Like a velvet rope, the gate looks soft but is backed by collateral. An attacker who forks a thousand fake agents must post a thousand separate bonds, so the cost rises with the tide of new accounts. When a fake is caught, its stake is slashed and burned, leaving a mesa of sunk capital. Mass identity becomes expensive, not free.
